spec.description:
# Starknet Validator Attestation Dashboard

This is a Grafana dashboard for monitoring Starknet validator attestations.

It visualizes the Prometheus metrics exposed by the [eqlabs/starknet-validator-attestation](https://github.com/eqlabs/starknet-validator-attestation) tool.

**Metrics displayed**

- Starknet latest block number
- Epoch progress (%)
- Blocks remaining until attestation
- Time since last successful attestation
- Success rate (%)
- Number of submitted, confirmed, and failed attestations (time series)
- Epoch Start Block
- Current Epoch ID
- Epoch Length
- Assigned Block
- Operational account balance (STRK)

## Setup

To use this dashboard:
1. Make sure your validator attestation tool is running and exposing metrics on a port, for example:
```
--metrics-address 127.0.0.1:9095
```
2. Add a job to your prometheus.yml file so that Prometheus scrapes metrics from the corresponding port(s) of your attestation tool instance(s), for example:
```
- job_name: "starknet-attestation"
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['localhost:9095']
      - targets: ['localhost:9096']
    relabel_configs:
      - source_labels: [__address__]
        regex: localhost:9095
        target_label: exported_network
        replacement: SN_MAIN
      - source_labels: [__address__]
        regex: localhost:9096
        target_label: exported_network
        replacement: SN_SEPOLIA
```
3. After updating the configuration, restart Prometheus. It will begin collecting and storing metrics for visualization and analysis.
4. Add Prometheus as a data source in Grafana.
5. Import the starknet-attestation-dashboard.json file in your Grafana UI.

That's it.

The three cumulative counters the attestation tool keeps, one set of lines per selected network. Submitted is what left the tool, confirmed is what the chain accepted, observed is the confirmations the tool saw. All three should sit on top of each other; the panel exists to catch them separating. What observed counts beyond confirmed has not been established - over a 12-hour window on 30 August 2026 the two matched exactly, 12 and 12 on mainnet, 111 and 111 on Sepolia. A gap of one or two out of several hundred is invisible here; the panel Submitted minus confirmed in Diagnostics shows that gap directly. A drop to zero means the attestation tool was restarted - the counters start again, the attestations themselves are not lost. The mainnet epoch is about an hour and the Sepolia epoch about six minutes, so the Sepolia lines climb roughly nine times faster.
spec.title: Attestations submitted, confirmed and observed

spec.description: One dot per event; zero values are filtered out, so an empty panel means nothing went wrong. A single missed epoch produces about thirty failure records, because the tool retries the transaction every 50 ms until the attestation window closes. Dot height is the count, but the height ratio between the two series carries no meaning.
spec.title: Failures & Missed Epochs

spec.description: Epochs that ended without a confirmed attestation, counted over the last day and the last week. On mainnet one missed epoch is money; on Sepolia it is a testnet event only. Zero on both lines is the normal reading.
spec.title: Missed epochs

spec.description: Confirmed attestations divided by confirmed plus missed epochs, computed over a sliding 24-hour window. The single number in the top row answers 'how is it now'; this line answers 'has it been slipping'. The dashed line is 99.5 percent, the threshold the alert rule uses. On mainnet a single miss drops the line to about 96 percent for a full day, because only about 24 epochs fit in 24 hours.
spec.title: Success rate over time, rolling 24h

spec.description: Share of the last day during which Prometheus could reach the attestation tool. Below 100 percent means the tool was down or unreachable for part of the day, which does not by itself mean an epoch was lost — check missed epochs for that.
spec.title: Attestation service uptime, 24h

spec.description: Time since the last confirmed attestation, divided by two epoch lengths. The Delay alert fires at 1.0, so this panel shows how much headroom is left. Normal teeth reach 0.85 to 0.92, which means the margin is under ten percent and a single slow epoch can produce a warning without any epoch being lost. Epoch length in seconds is not a constant here: it is the length in blocks divided by the block rate measured over the last hour from the chain head, so the panel follows the network if it changes pace. Right after the attestation tool restarts the rate needs a few minutes of history before this reads correctly. Values above 10000 are dropped: before the first attestation of a fresh tool the timestamp metric is zero, and the expression would otherwise draw a spike of millions.
spec.title: Delay in units of two epochs

spec.description: The same value the top row shows as a number, drawn over time. Each tooth is one epoch: the line climbs while waiting and drops to zero the moment an attestation is confirmed. A tooth that keeps climbing past the usual height is the shape of a missed epoch.
spec.title: Minutes since last attestation

spec.description: Starknet changes this parameter on its own, so it is not a constant. Mainnet has been seen at 2088, 2118 and 2123 blocks. Every threshold derived from epoch length — both Delay alerts — is only valid while this line stays where it was when they were computed, so a visible step here is a reason to recompute them.
spec.title: Epoch length in blocks

spec.description: Where inside the epoch the network placed the block this validator must attest, as a percentage of epoch length. The position is random by design and should scatter across the whole range. A value near 100 means the assignment landed at the very end of the epoch, which is when a slow gateway is most likely to cost the epoch.
spec.title: Assigned block position within epoch

spec.description: Balance a day ago minus balance now. Measured over 12 hours on 30 August this came to about 15 STRK a day on mainnet and about 160 on Sepolia, the difference being that the Sepolia epoch is nine times shorter. A top-up during the window makes this read zero, not a negative number.
spec.title: STRK spent, last 24h

spec.description: Spending over the last day divided by the attestations confirmed in it. This is the unit cost of one attestation and it should be nearly the same on both networks; a rise on one of them means transactions there got more expensive or more of them were retried.
spec.title: STRK per confirmed attestation, 24h

spec.description: Attestations sent to the network that have not been confirmed. A flat line is healthy whatever its height; the height itself is history since the tool started. Each step up is one attestation that went out and did not come back. The line falls to zero when the attestation tool restarts.
spec.title: Submitted minus confirmed

spec.description: Counted as the number of times the confirmed-attestation counter went backwards, which only happens when the tool restarts. A restart resets every cumulative counter on this dashboard, so a non-zero number here explains why the long lines dropped to zero.
spec.title: Attestation tool restarts, 24h

spec.description: Epochs the network completed in the last day minus attestations confirmed in it. Zero means every epoch was attested. The two are separate event streams: an epoch boundary is a moment on chain, while a confirmation lands at a random block inside the epoch, so the edge of a 24-hour window can catch one more or one less of either. A reading of 1 is that boundary effect, not a missed epoch. Measured twice 50 seconds apart on 5 September 2026, the raw value moved from -1 to 0 with nothing changing on chain. Negative results are clamped to zero, because a negative count of unattested epochs has no meaning. The colour turns only at 2 and above. The tool's own count is in Missed epochs; this panel is the independent cross-check that would catch an epoch the tool did not notice at all.
spec.title: Epochs without attestation, 24h

spec.description: How many blocks the local node is behind the head of the chain. Normal is 0 to 2. The attestation tool reads block numbers from this node, so a node that falls behind attests late or not at all. This panel reads metrics of the pathfinder node, not of the attestation tool. Those metrics carry the label network with values mainnet and testnet-sepolia, while the attestation metrics use exported_network with SN_MAIN and SN_SEPOLIA. The Network variable holds a value that matches both vocabularies at once, so this panel follows the selection like the rest of the dashboard.
spec.title: Node sync lag

spec.description: Requests from the node to the Starknet gateway that timed out; zero values are filtered out, so an empty panel means there were none. This is the failure reason that mattered in both real block stalls seen so far — the constant background of the other reason, starknet, is deliberately not drawn here. A cluster of dots at the same minute as a missed epoch is the evidence that the cause was outside this server. This panel reads metrics of the pathfinder node, not of the attestation tool. Those metrics carry the label network with values mainnet and testnet-sepolia, while the attestation metrics use exported_network with SN_MAIN and SN_SEPOLIA. The Network variable holds a value that matches both vocabularies at once, so this panel follows the selection like the rest of the dashboard.
spec.title: Gateway timeouts

spec.description: Normal is about 35 on each network. A drop to 2 or 3 followed by a burst above 70 is a real stall: the node was not getting blocks and then caught up. A dip to 15 or 20 without a burst is the chain itself producing fewer blocks, which is not a fault. This panel reads metrics of the pathfinder node, not of the attestation tool. Those metrics carry the label network with values mainnet and testnet-sepolia, while the attestation metrics use exported_network with SN_MAIN and SN_SEPOLIA. The Network variable holds a value that matches both vocabularies at once, so this panel follows the selection like the rest of the dashboard.
spec.title: Blocks received per minute by the node

spec.description: Clock time of the last moment in the past day when the node stopped receiving blocks, or OK if there was no such moment. The same panel exists on the node dashboard; it is repeated here because a lost epoch is explained on this dashboard and the answer usually lies in that number. This panel reads metrics of the pathfinder node, not of the attestation tool. Those metrics carry the label network with values mainnet and testnet-sepolia, while the attestation metrics use exported_network with SN_MAIN and SN_SEPOLIA. The Network variable holds a value that matches both vocabularies at once, so this panel follows the selection like the rest of the dashboard.
spec.title: Node stall, last 24h

spec.description: Confirmed attestations over confirmed plus missed, across the last week. The delegation program requires 99 percent liveness on both networks, so this is the number that matters for it rather than the daily one.
spec.title: Success rate, 7d

spec.description: The same ratio over a month. It becomes meaningful once a month of history has accumulated in the local Prometheus, which starts on 27 August 2026. On a shorter history the ratio itself is still correct - numerator and denominator are computed over the same range - but it covers only the history that exists, not the full 30 days. This panel exists on the local Grafana only: Grafana Cloud keeps 14 days, so a 30-day window is unreachable there.
spec.title: Success rate, 30d

spec.description: The raw counter, not a windowed figure. It resets to zero when the attestation tool restarts, so it counts since the last restart rather than since the validator was set up.
spec.title: Missed epochs since tool start

spec.description: Solid line is the balance; the second series is a straight-line projection thirty days out, fitted on the last six hours of spending. The projection is only as good as that fit — it assumes the pace does not change and does not know about top-ups. Useful for one question: does the balance reach the alert threshold within the month.
spec.title: Balance with 30-day projection

spec.description: Days until the balance reaches 500 STRK, the level at which the Operational Account Balance Low rule fires on mainnet, at the last day's rate of spending. Sepolia has its own level of 20000 and this panel does not account for it, so read the Sepolia value as informational only. Capped at 9999 when spending is near zero.
spec.title: Days until the balance alert fires

spec.description: Seconds since the current epoch started, computed from the block count and the block rate measured over the last hour, so no block time is hardwired. Mainnet epochs run about 60 minutes and Sepolia about 6.4. Right after the attestation tool restarts the rate needs a few minutes of history before this reads correctly.
spec.title: Time in epoch

spec.description: Confirmed attestations over confirmed plus missed, across the last 90 days. This is the window the StarkWare delegation program states: 99 percent liveness on mainnet and testnet. Local Prometheus starts on 27 August 2026, so a full 90-day window is only available from late November 2026; before that the panel covers whatever history exists. The ratio itself stays correct on a short window, because numerator and denominator are computed over the same range - only the absolute counts are partial. This panel exists on the local Grafana only: Grafana Cloud keeps 14 days of history, so there it could never read correctly.
spec.title: Success rate, 90d

spec.description: Epochs that ended without a confirmed attestation over the last 90 days. This is the count behind the 90-day success rate next to it. Mainnet runs about one epoch an hour, so a 90-day window holds roughly 2160 epochs and the 99 percent floor allows about 21 misses; Sepolia runs about nine times faster and its budget is correspondingly larger, which is why this panel is left uncoloured - one colour scale cannot serve both networks. Same history caveat as the 90-day success rate: local Prometheus starts on 27 August 2026.
spec.title: Missed epochs, 90d

spec.description: Confirmed attestations over confirmed plus missed, across the last fourteen days. The delegation program requires 99 percent liveness on both networks, so this is the number that matters for it. Fourteen days is the retention of Grafana Cloud on the free plan, which is why this window exists: on a store that keeps only two weeks it is the longest honest window. It sits right at the edge of that retention, so the coverage can fall a few hours short of the full fourteen days; the ratio itself stays correct either way, because numerator and denominator are computed over the same range.
spec.title: Success rate, 14d
Validator Attestation Monitoring

spec.description: Pick the Prometheus data source that holds these metrics. Every panel on this dashboard reads it from here, so nothing needs editing panel by panel.
spec.label: Data source
spec.name: ds
